correctness.rationale: An invertible integer A=[[-2,-1,3],[-1,0,-3],[0,-2,1]] has determinant 17. For each enforced row i, the two projected remaining normals span the residual plane; p=a/(a+b), q=1-p, z=d^2/(ab) in [0,1). The projected line annihilators T,U satisfy TUT=zT, UTU=zU. The first-step M1=pT+qU has max eigenvalue (1+sqrt(1-4pq(1-z)))/2. The second-step M2=(p^2+pqz)T+(q^2+pqz)U has the claimed eigenvalue formula, and its two-coefficient positive recursion has Perron root rho=(1+sqrt((p-q)^2+4pq z^2))/2 for nonzero z. Independent exact rational Gram computations reproduced the source p,z values (91/136,7/585), (91/132,841/3731), (45/86,80/369), and separate radical comparisons prove L1(1)<L3(1)<L2(1) while L3(2)<L1(2)<L2(2); row 3 minimizes rho as well. Strict inequalities ensure openness. For nonsingular 2x2 and one fixed hard row, the one remaining projected row annihilates the one-dimensional error in one update; hence dimension three is minimal. Minimax is over different hard-row-specific unit initial errors, NOT over a single common initialization.

value.rationale: This is a motivated, smallest-dimension discrete hard-equation selection reversal in a known preconditioned randomized algorithm. It cautions that optimizing a one-step minimax loss, even with exactly computable projected row weights, can select a different hard equation than two-step or long-run criteria. The exact integer witness, dimension barrier and open stability provide a nontrivial counterexample and structural boundary without claiming a new general MSE formula.
